eulob


Overview

eulob is an R package for exploring lobbying organisations across Europe through EU-LOB, an open and continuously expanding database. It brings together records from the European Union Transparency Register, national and regional lobbying and transparency registers, and publicly documented meetings with institutional representatives.

The package provides tools to search, retrieve, and compare organisations across different sources and jurisdictions. Its exact and approximate name-matching methods help identify potential correspondences between records despite differences in naming conventions or spelling.

Available lobbying registers

The catalogue covers 19 territorial scopes and 21 lobbying registers.

Code Country / Territory Lobbying register
AT Austria Austrian Lobbying Register
BE Belgium Belgian Chamber Lobby Register
CY Cyprus Cyprus Lobbying Register
CZ Czech Republic Czech RELOB
DE Germany German Lobby Register
EE Estonia Estonian Lobby Meetings
ES Spain Spanish CNMC Interest Groups Register
FI Finland Finnish Transparency Register
FR France French HATVP Register
GR Greece Greek Lobbying Register
IE Ireland Irish Register of Lobbying
IT Italy Camera dei Deputati
IT Italy Italian MIMIT Register
IT Italy Tuscany Interest Groups Register
LT Lithuania Lithuanian Lobbyists Register
LU Luxembourg Luxembourg Chamber Interest Representatives
LV Latvia Latvian Lobbying Register
PL Poland Polish Professional Lobbying Register
RO Romania Romanian Lobbying Register
UE European Union EU Transparency Register
UK United Kingdom UK Consultant Lobbyists Register

The code UE represents the supranational EU Transparency Register and is not an ISO country code.

Historical records from the Netherlands (NL) are retained outside the searchable catalogue because the available source does not reliably identify individual lobbying entities.

Use eulob_registers() to inspect the available registers.

Installation

Development version (GitHub)

The development version of eulob is available from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github(
  "AritzUMA/eulob",
  build = FALSE,
  upgrade = "never"
)

To check the installed version:

library(eulob)
packageVersion("eulob")

GitHub contains the latest development version selected for public release. Additional changes may be under development in the GitLab repository.

CRAN release

Version 0.2.1 has been submitted to CRAN and is awaiting review. Once accepted and published, the released version can be installed with:

install.packages("eulob")

Getting started

Load the package:

library(eulob)

List available countries and registers:

eulob_countries()
eulob_registers()

Explore the Spanish register:

eulob_registers(country = "ES")
head(eulob_lobbies(country = "ES"))

Search for organizations:

eulob_search("association", limit = 10)
eulob_search("universidad", country = "UE", limit = 10)

Inspect package metadata:

eulob_info()
eulob_version()

Main functions

  • eulob_countries(): territorial coverage and counts.
  • eulob_registers(): available lobbying registers.
  • eulob_sources(): register-level catalogue counts.
  • eulob_lobbies(): names and register-specific identifiers.
  • eulob_get(): retrieve entries using a register identifier.
  • eulob_search(): literal and approximate name searches.
  • eulob_search_normalized(): normalized-name candidate retrieval.
  • eulob_cross_registers(): names shared across registers.
  • eulob_info(): package information.
  • eulob_version(): installed package version.

Data structure

The bundled catalogue contains 40,482 normalized name records, 42,599 name-to-register-identifier relationships and 42,265 distinct country-register-identifier keys.

These relationships do not necessarily represent distinct legal entities.

The name_id field identifies a normalized name. The lobby_id field contains a source-specific key. Depending on the register, this may be an official identifier or a synthetic identifier derived from the source data.

Records can represent different source-level units, including registrations, participant strings and individual persons. They should not all be interpreted as independently verified lobbying organizations.

Search limitations

The default eulob_search() method uses cosine similarity over character bigrams. Alternative methods include Jaccard, Jaro-Winkler, Damerau-Levenshtein and case-insensitive literal substring matching (method = "fixed").

The similarity methods compare textual denominations rather than semantic representations. High similarity, or the presence of an identical name in multiple registers, does not establish that records refer to the same legal entity. The package does not perform verified cross-register legal entity resolution.

Reproducibility

The catalogue is bundled with the package. Collection dates, data provenance and independent catalogue versioning must be documented before the first CRAN submission.
